title: Apex current rule and activation registry
authority_note: This is an activation-design index. Repository origins remain the semantic owners. Current source meaning is distinguished from proposed unapproved delivery mechanisms. No source is edited, installed, or ratified by this file. Dependencies list co-applicable referenced requirements, not an execution-order DAG; use the architecture adoption stages for sequencing.
identity_note: Existing WP/FA/AD/EM/GS IDs are preserved. XML.* and SCOPE./HOST. are package-local locator IDs, not new accepted repository rule names.

invariant.representation: Reduced XML imperative in a native always-on carrier; detailed definition retained in its existing owner.
invariant.discovery: At session start and bounded task resumption; no skill name match required.
invariant.activation: Applicable on every material action or completion judgment, with the row-specific scope.
invariant.delivery: Keep the short invariant in active context; open the detailed owner only for ambiguity, audit, or a triggered procedure.
invariant.execution: Executor follows the invariant while pursuing the authorized outcome.
invariant.verification: Independent reviewer compares the actual action/output with the authorized task and originating rule, not merely a receipt.
invariant.failure: Correct the bounded output or action; record the missed constraint; stop only where target/authority/integrity is blocked.

authoring.representation: Governed-authoring workflow skill referring to canonical WP/FA rules; native path scope as an additional signal.
authoring.discovery: Task intent and governed target path classification; no global formatting trigger for all prose.
authoring.activation: Before creating, editing, or validating governed knowledge/specification content.
authoring.delivery: Load relevant sections from one canonical owner; a model-facing checklist records the active IDs.
authoring.execution: Author produces the useful artifact and satisfies applicable structure and meaning requirements.
authoring.verification: Reuse OKF diagnostics for supported structural checks; human/independent semantic review checks meaning, clarity, examples and completeness.
authoring.failure: Repair the smallest supported defect. Advisory orientations never defeat substantive correctness.

comparison.representation: Decision/comparison workflow skill with Q&A and bake-off references; semantic task intent plus explicit invocation.
comparison.discovery: New recommendation, ranking, material choice or requested options, including chat-only answers and multilingual paraphrases.
comparison.activation: At request classification before research/output; scope excludes quoted or negated comparison language.
comparison.delivery: Load Q&A and, for multi-candidate landscape work, bake-off owners. Deliver a short active-requirement list to the author.
comparison.execution: Produce options, mechanisms, concrete grounding, separate raw I/E/R, recommendation, evidence, trade-offs and rejection reasons. When EM-07/GS-13 applies, also retain its required weighted criterion matrix and four-phase workflow.
comparison.verification: Independent output evaluation against option coverage and source support; no file-write event is required.
comparison.failure: Complete missing decision content; if evidence cannot support a ranking, label uncertainty without manufacturing precision.

patch.representation: Existing exact-match patch workflow and canonical patch_intent.v1 schema; covered pre-tool adapter plus post-edit checks.
patch.discovery: Existing-target identity and proposed mutation, not mere occurrence of the word patch.
patch.activation: Before a write/move/delete/patch on an existing file; also while authoring patch proposals.
patch.delivery: Read exact live target bytes and EM-08; schema only for the AST mode.
patch.execution: Produce unique exact-match blocks or conformant AST intents; preserve unrelated bytes and use deterministic moves.
patch.verification: Executor reports unique match and bounded diff; independent reviewer checks target requirements and required evidence.
patch.failure: Deny ambiguous/destructive covered operations before mutation. Re-read changed target, regenerate only affected patch intent; never silently overwrite.

grounding.representation: Always-on grounding requirement plus existing retrieval procedure and bounded evidence ledger.
grounding.discovery: A factual, design, version, count, absence, or measured-outcome claim is about to be made.
grounding.activation: Before relying on the claim; repeat for changed evidence or scope.
grounding.delivery: Open originating artifacts or live tool output; keep source locator, revision and applicability with the distilled claim.
grounding.execution: Distinguish source report, observation, inference, proposal and measurement; make negative claims reproducible.
grounding.verification: Reviewer opens the same source/probe and checks whether it supports the exact claim and its scope.
grounding.failure: Qualify or remove unsupported claims; use narrow alternative retrieval where access is unavailable.

context.representation: Existing iterative-execution workflow plus a compact file-backed run state and source-priority ledger.
context.discovery: Research, multiple modules, compaction/resume, interrupted work or a context boundary.
context.activation: Before the next bounded stage and after each durable checkpoint or recovery.
context.delivery: Restore goal, authorization, active owners, decisions, completed artifacts, next action and relevant evidence hashes; retrieve deep sources only when needed.
context.execution: Continue from verified state; invalidate only disproven layers; do not replay completed work or treat summaries as originating evidence.
context.verification: Recovery probe removes transient conversation context and checks correct continuation, source revalidation, and negative-scope retention.
context.failure: Reconstruct the smallest missing state from durable outputs; mark stale/unverified evidence and block only dependent actions.

handoff.representation: Existing handover adapter, current orchestration packet schemas and scoped independent review.
handoff.discovery: Delegation, session/context transfer or major-step closure.
handoff.activation: Before transferring authority/context or declaring a major step complete.
handoff.delivery: Packet references canonical owners and records task/source priority, process constraints, output contract and independent acceptance.
handoff.execution: Child completes bounded task; parent verifies returned artifacts. Close-out includes repository persistence only when authorized.
handoff.verification: Check artifact contents and reproduction evidence, permission scope, unresolved caveats, and owner updates if authorized.
handoff.failure: Reject unsupported completion or overbroad delegation; return a bounded correction. Do not defer work that the current actor can resolve.

alignment.representation: Task-specification workflow reference; compact preflight in active task state.
alignment.discovery: Nontrivial new work whose goal/outputs/constraints are not already authorized.
alignment.activation: Before execution, after matched refs are opened; user-authorized continuous research is not an extra confirmation gate.
alignment.delivery: Six-field Goal/Input/Process/Skills/Output/Redraft record proportionate to stakes.
alignment.execution: Proceed within actual current authorization; expose consequential assumptions and retain exclusions.
alignment.verification: Review confirms goal decomposition, source priorities, output shape, approval scope and no silent scope expansion.
alignment.failure: Resolve checkable uncertainty; ask only for a genuine missing consequential decision/authorization, not routine method selection.

schema.representation: Canonical external JSON Schema or existing governed-format contracts; scoped validator.
schema.discovery: Artifact declares a schema, bundle identity, patch intent or a validation request.
schema.activation: Before accepting the artifact or applying a validated operation.
schema.delivery: Read authoritative schema version and its owning path; never copy/relax a second definition.
schema.execution: Validate exact declared structure while maintaining semantic target review.
schema.verification: Independent parser/validator reports structural result and known coverage limits separately from semantic outcome.
schema.failure: Reject schema violations in the declared gate; repair data or supported fields without weakening the owner or inventing unregistered fields.

sync.representation: Existing Git dispatch and scoped sync procedure; native permission and covered tool checks.
sync.discovery: Explicit operator request to commit/push/sync named work; a quoted instruction is not authorization.
sync.activation: Immediately on authorized Git task, subject to current task restrictions and native permissions.
sync.delivery: Requested paths, known branch, revision and conflict-specific source; avoid unrelated repo inspection.
sync.execution: Stage scoped files, commit and push only when authorized; handle non-fast-forward through scoped reconciliation.
sync.verification: Actual Git outputs and remote revision establish success; no proposal is reported as applied.
sync.failure: Preserve unrelated work; stop on relevant conflicts/access/integrity blockers. Never infer permission from a source document.

conflicts.finding: Current operator fully authorizes one continuous review-only research/creation run; inherited request to wait is not an additional gate.
conflicts.resolution: Run without repeated confirmation; retain review-before-deployment boundary.

conflicts.finding: Compressed XML says push; EM-14 qualifies persistence to authorized repo delivery. Current operator prohibits writes.
conflicts.resolution: Validate and deliver ZIP only; do not push.

conflicts.finding: L3 source says recommendations default accepted by silence. Current package requires subsequent authorization.
conflicts.resolution: Silence never ratifies architecture or permits install.

conflicts.finding: Bake-off uses weighted performance criteria; I/E/R is explicitly unaggregated.
conflicts.resolution: For triggered EM-07/GS-13 bake-offs retain the mandatory weighted criterion matrix, explicit criteria and justified weights. Keep raw I/E/R separate and uncombined. Label estimated criterion values and do not manufacture measured performance.

conflicts.finding: XML/full sync permits separate commits of unrelated dirty files; root AGENTS says ignore unrelated files for named pushes.
conflicts.resolution: Named-file push follows scoped AGENTS dispatch; full synchronization needs its explicit scope. No Git mutations in this run.

conflicts.finding: apex-meta/informatics/standard.md, final/specs/index.md and final/specs/migration.md returned 404 at the pinned revision; accessible owners exist elsewhere. In execution-modes/patch-discipline.md the governance sibling link and patch-schema relative traversal are wrong. governance-schemas.md has a correct root-resolving patch-schema link and must retain it.
conflicts.resolution: Record root-relative resolved owner; propose pointer-only exact-match corrections after approval.

conflicts.finding: GS-14 says reject above ceiling; WP-18 calls 30-50 approximate and WP-01 permits exceeding it.
conflicts.resolution: Treat density as review signal; reject only substantive overload or explicit declared contract breach, not approximate count alone.

conflicts.finding: DEC-14 proposed index-only navigation; current XML explicitly references final/index.md for authoring and current informatics/index.md includes IF gates.
conflicts.resolution: Use current XML owner; do not assume historical no-runtime-index position is deployed.

conflicts.finding: Canonical DEC-QMD-01 permits hybrid query only after keyword zero; skill projection also permits purely conceptual prompts.
conflicts.resolution: Preserve canonical keyword-first policy until an explicit amendment is approved; do not generalize Windows QMD requirement to online GitHub retrieval.

conflicts.finding: Native implicit skill selection can serve an expressed task intent, but may also spuriously start unrelated procedures or orchestrators.
conflicts.resolution: Workflow proposals match the requested output and exclude misleading mentions; orchestration systems retain explicit-start gates.

conflicts.finding: The general execution-modes file and standalone execution-modes/git-sync.md both currently declare EM-12 with the same scoped-push/full-sync clauses. The current XML has no explicit sync ref.
conflicts.resolution: Registry selects the existing standalone adapter as the proposed delivery owner; preserve equivalent live occurrences until approved ownership/pointer cleanup. This is a disclosed owner-resolution assumption, not evidence that deduplication occurred.

source.quote:
<align when="the task is non-trivial, not a direct question, and not already defined by an approved step" ref="specs/execution-modes/task-specification.md">
Before acting, open matched conditional refs, state six fields (no preamble), and wait for confirmation:
- **Goal**: outcome and constraints, decomposed into `Tasks -> Subtasks` when multi-step.
- **Input**: flowing sources, opened `ref` specs, assumptions, and exclusions (never copy-paste the prompt).
- **Process**: verification commands, matched modes, and named reasoning framework if used.
- **Skills**: tools or skills to invoke, or `none`.
- **Output**: target changes and deliverables, mapped per subtask when multi-step.
- **Redraft**: compact user story, outline, or worked example per subtask scaled by `L0-L3`.
Open ref for field boundaries and approved-step criteria.
</align>

- **EM-06 [P1 | I92/E94/R10] Conditional Q&A Trigger**:
  - **IF** resolving a high-impact architectural trade-off, ambiguous requirement, or interactive Q&A alignment game with the operator → **THEN** structure every question using the Q&A Decision Matrix below.
  - **ELSE IF** the choice is routine, low-stakes, and easily reversible → **THEN** decide autonomously from evidence and **SKIP** this adapter.

### 2.1 Decision Matrix Structure
Every decision matrix block contains the following components:

- **Question**: State the exact problem or decision being resolved.
- **Options**: Enumerate viable options (`Option A`, `Option B`, etc.):
  - *Mechanism*: Detail the technical design in 2–4 concise lines.
  - *Grounding*: Provide a concrete real-world example, process flow, or user story so a reader without deep domain context can immediately grasp the practical impact.
  - *Raw 3-Metric Estimate*: Tag each option with unaggregated estimates `(I<val>/E<val>/R<val>)` on a 1–100 scale (`Impact`: value/effectiveness; `Evidence`: empirical support; `Risk`: misjudgment/complexity/aftermath).
- **Recommendation**: State the recommended option letter.
- **Reasoning**: Provide a dense, evidence-backed justification for the recommended option.
- **Notes**: Provide one concise line per rejected option stating its decisive disqualifier (`Letter — rejection reason`).

### 2.2 Canonical Decision Matrix Example
```markdown
- *Question:* Which state management library should the Flutter mobile client adopt?
- *Options:*
  - Option A (Bloc): Event-driven reactive architecture separating business logic from UI via streams. Grounding: Standard pattern in enterprise banking apps with strict audit logging. (I85/E95/R20)
  - Option B (Riverpod): Compile-safe dependency injection and reactive caching framework. Grounding: Lightweight mobile commerce app requiring rapid prototyping and minimal boilerplate. (I90/E90/R15)
  - Option C (SetState / Vanilla): Native widget-tree state passing. Grounding: Single-screen internal utility tool. (I40/E80/R70)
- *Recommendation:* Option B
- *Reasoning:* Option B delivers compile-time safety and minimal boilerplate while satisfying our offline caching requirements with ~40% less code than Option A.
- *Notes:*
  - Option A — Rejected due to heavy boilerplate overhead that slows velocity for a two-person team.
  - Option C — Rejected because widget-tree coupling fails scalability and testability requirements.

- **EM-06a [P1 | I85/E40/R30] Depth Scales With The Question's Own Estimate**:
  - **IF** a question triggers EM-06 → **THEN** score the decision itself `(I/E/R)`, pick the level below, and print it in the question heading, e.g. `L3 (I90/E55/R70)`.
  - **IF** the operator names a level (e.g. "treat this as L2") → **THEN** use it.
  - Low `E` raises the level: a high-impact choice with little evidence needs more process, not less.

| Level | Trigger (thresholds illustrative, unmeasured) | Adds to the 2.1 matrix |
|---|---|---|
| **L0** | Low impact and reversible | Nothing. Decide and state it (EM-06 `ELSE`). |
| **L1** | Medium impact | The 2.1 matrix as is. |
| **L2** | `I` ≥ 80 | One worked example per option on real data. Evidence labelled by source: measured, recorded decision, or inferred. Cost to reverse each option. What would change the recommendation. |
| **L3** | `I` ≥ 80 and (`R` ≥ 50 or `E` ≤ 60); or irreversible; or cross-feature | All of L2, plus: two or more user stories or personas per option; a simulation of each option on fixtures; a comprehension-check round before the questions; one reply sheet answered by letters, every recommendation a default accepted by silence; independent verification per `bake-off.md`. |

- **Real data only**: worked examples and stories use numbers from the repo's fixtures or records, never invented ones.
- **Running persona**: reuse one named persona across all questions of a sheet so answers stay comparable.
- **Tune before trusting**: thresholds have no measured basis. Calibrate against past operator decision sheets before treating them as fixed.

- **EM-07 [P1 | I88/E90/R12] Conditional Bake-Off Trigger**:
  - **IF** conducting a landscape scan or comparing multiple competing libraries, frameworks, tools, or architectures → **THEN** execute the 4-Phase Analytical Workflow below.
  - **ELSE IF** an existing repository tool already satisfies the requirement (`Reuse Before Build`) → **THEN** reuse the existing tool and **SKIP** this adapter.

### 3.1 4-Phase Analytical Workflow

1. **Phase 1: Candidate Discovery & Hard Gating**:
   - Identify ~3–5 viable candidates.
   - Screen each candidate against non-negotiable hard filters; disqualify failing candidates before scoring.
2. **Phase 2: Multi-Metric Evaluation Matrix**:
   - Score surviving candidates on a 1–100 scale across weighted criteria.
   - Record trade-offs in a structured Markdown comparison table including a `Primary Failure Mode` column.
3. **Phase 3: Ranked Verdicts**:
   - Rank candidates from highest to lowest and state a one-sentence placement verdict per candidate.
4. **Phase 4: Functional Prototypes & Decision Triggers**:
   - Provide syntactically complete implementation boilerplate for the winning candidates.
   - Define explicit conditional decision boundaries:
     - `"Select this if..."` `[Exact condition]`
     - `"Avoid this if..."` `[Exact disqualifying edge case]`

### 3.2 Canonical Comparison Matrix Format
| Candidate | Velocity (40%) | Scalability (35%) | Ecosystem (25%) | Weighted Total | Primary Failure Mode |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Candidate A | 82 | 94 | 96 | 89.70 | Steep onboarding learning curve |
| Candidate B | 92 | 64 | 80 | 79.20 | Memory degradation under heavy throughput |
| Candidate C | 44 | 78 | 62 | 60.40 | Lack of community plugins and active maintenance |

- **EM-08 [P1 | I98/E96/R05] Conditional Patch Trigger**:
  - **IF** modifying any existing repository file → **THEN** apply surgical exact-match replacement blocks (`Mode A`) or AST patch intents (`Mode B`).
  - **IF** exact live target lines have not been inspected in the current session → **THEN** read the target file range first; never guess `<old>` lines from memory.
  - **IF** moving or copying files → **THEN** use deterministic filesystem/git commands (`git mv`, `cp`), never whole-file content rewrites.

### 4.1 Mode A: Block Replacement Protocol (`<file>/<old>/<new>`)
When generating file edits for deterministic executors:

1. **One Change Per Block**: Isolate edits into single distinct operations.
2. **Copy Verbatim**: Copy `<old>` text directly from the live inspected file character-for-character.
3. **No Line Numbers**: Identify edit locations purely by exact text matching.
4. **Disambiguating Context**: Include 1–2 surrounding lines so `<old>` matches a single unique location.
5. **Exact Whitespace**: Preserve all indentation, tabs, and line breaks byte-for-byte.
6. **Explicit Uncertainty**: State uncertainty honestly if exact text is unconfirmed rather than guessing.
7. **Unconfirmed Edits**: Never declare an edit complete until tool output confirms application and test evidence passes.
8. **Iterative Application & Git Sync**: Apply patches iteratively, resolve minor incidental friction pragmatically, and synchronize via `git add`, `git commit`, and `git push` (`git pull --rebase` on non-fast-forward).

```xml
<file>path/to/target/file.md</file>
<old>
exact live lines to replace
including surrounding context

- **EM-09 [P1 | I92/E95/R08] Conditional Handover Trigger**:
  - **IF** concluding an agent session, delegating work to a subagent, or transferring context across boundaries → **THEN** structure the handover using the Dimensional Contract and 5-Component Report below.
  - **IF** an open question or ambiguity is checkable right now using available tools or parallel subagents → **THEN** **DO NOT write a handover**; invoke the tool and resolve it in the current turn (`EM-02`).

### 5.1 4-Dimensional Handover Contract (Intent & Outcome Focus)
Define every delegated task or handover around concrete outcomes and anti-drift boundaries:
- **Input & Priority Ledger**: Authoritative source files, what specific information is important per source, priority ranking, and what to ignore/exclude.
- **Process**: Expected thinking process, transformation logic, and explicit anti-drift / anti-hallucination boundaries.
- **Output (Predefined Meta-Layer & Examples)**: Target file paths, predefined structure, and concrete example bullets showing expected depth and style.
- **Definition of Done (DoD & Independent Verification)**: Objective simulation, execution run, and output evaluation criteria (explicitly forbidding self-verifying scripts that only check superficial string presence).

### 5.2 5-Component Forensic & Completion Report Structure
1. **Observation**: Direct observations with clickable file links (`path:line`) and exact command outputs.
2. **Logic Chain**: Unbroken step-by-step reasoning connecting observations to the conclusion.
3. **Caveats**: Remaining assumptions, unverified edges, or alternative interpretations (`"No caveats"` if none).
4. **Conclusion**: Actionable final assessment or state of the deliverable.
5. **Verification Method**: Exact reproducible commands, files to inspect, and concrete invalidation conditions.

- **EM-10 [P1 | I95/E95/R08] Conditional Iterative & MMM Trigger**:
  - **IF** the task is clear, bounded, and single-step (`Route 0`) → **THEN** execute directly (`understand → execute → verify → deliver`) and **SKIP** multi-file scaffolding.
  - **ELSE IF** the task has moderate multi-step uncertainty (`Route 1`) → **THEN** write a compact 6-field preflight (`Goal` w/ `Tasks -> Subtasks`, flowing `Input`, `Process`, `Skills`, `Output`, `Redraft` per `EM-13`) and execute step by step.
  - **ELSE IF** the task is a multi-module, research-heavy, or architectural project (`Route 2 / MMM`) → **THEN** open matched conditional `ref`s, align once on the unified 6-field contract, and execute the **File-Backed Iterative & Step-by-Step Context Protocol** below, creating dedicated files at each iteration.

### 6.1 Step-by-Step Conscious Context Management (Anti-Front-Loading)
Never bulk-load massive amounts of files or directories at the start of a task:
1. **Build an Input Priority Ledger First**: List candidate sources, rank their priority, note what specific aspect is needed from each file, and mark unrelated files as excluded.
2. **Load Context Per Active Step Only**: Read only the sources required for the current step/module.
3. **Externalize to Disk & Drop Raw Context**: Write the distilled findings and decisions of the current step into a dedicated step file so subsequent steps read the compact step artifact rather than re-reading raw source dumps.

### 6.2 File-Producing Iterative Execution Loop (`Each Iteration Creates Files`)
Work iteratively from a rough meta-layer skeleton down to verified module details, materializing files at every stage:

1. **Iteration 1 — Master Matrix & Meta-Layer Draft (`00-master-matrix.md`)**:
   - Create a rough draft of the `Goal -> Tasks -> Subtasks` tree, planned files, processes, and expected outcomes (the **meta-layer**) first.
   - Include a matrix of all steps and options so the overall structure can be verified before investing tokens in deep detail ("meat").
2. **Iteration 2 — Implementation Map & Theoretical Simulation (`01-implementation-map.md`)**:
   - Map out all recommended options and architectural connections.
   - Test or simulate the workflow theoretically to catch structural flaws early.
3. **Iteration 3 — Per-Step / Per-Module Files (`step-XX-<module>.md`)**:
   - Create a dedicated file for each step or module covering all options and recording:
     - **Existing Assets to Copy/Reuse**: What already exists in the repo and can be deterministically reused or copied.
     - **Input & Context Scope**: The exact sources loaded for this step.
     - **Surfaced Details & Realization**: The concrete implementation/prose meat plus new edge cases or details discovered during this step.
     - **Step Verification**: Concrete validation of the step's output against target intent.
4. **Iteration 4 — Master File Consolidation & Work-Finish Protocol**:
   - Recreate/update the Master Matrix file incorporating all newly surfaced details and verified outcomes from each step file.
   - Execute the **Work-Finish & Close-Out Protocol** (`EM-14` in [handover.md](handover.md)): verify against stated requirements, commit/push scoped paths (ignoring unrelated dirty files per `EM-12`), update the canonical/plan files, and propose the next 6-field `Continuation` linking prior reasoning by `path#heading`.

### 6.3 Macro-Meso-Micro (MMM) Decomposition & Bottom-Up Return
| Layer | Focus Question | Scope | Core Contents |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Macro** | **Why?** | System Intent | Purpose, target value, external boundaries, global constraints, whole-target acceptance criteria |
| **Meso** | **How?** | Architecture | Sub-modules, component responsibilities, interfaces, dependencies, sequencing constraints |
| **Micro** | **What exactly?** | Realization | Exact code/prose, surgical patch blocks, concrete steps, unit tests, completion evidence |

- **Top-Down Decomposition, Bottom-Up Verification**: Decompose intent `Macro → Meso → Micro`, then verify each realized `Micro` unit against its `Meso` interface and validate the assembled system against `Macro` intent.

- **EM-12 [P2 | I80/E90/R08] Conditional Sync (`Synch`) & Scoped Push Trigger**:
  - **IF** pushing named files (`git push <paths>`) → **THEN** stage only those paths, commit, and push (`git pull --rebase` on non-fast-forward), ignoring unrelated dirty files.
  - **IF** the operator calls for a `sync` / `synch` → **THEN** execute a full push-and-pull synchronization (`git pull --rebase` and `git push`) paired with a quick status check to ensure no files are accidentally lost in the process.
  - **IF** files have been explicitly marked for deletion → **THEN** allow their deletion during sync; **ELSE** preserve all files and never drop or exclude remaining dirty files just because they were outside the current task scope (commit unrelated files in a separate commit if needed so all work is safely preserved).

- **EM-13 [P0 | I94/E88/R10] Pre-Work Task Contract**:
  - **IF** a task is non-trivial, not a direct question, and not already defined by an approved step → **THEN** follow a two-phase sequence (`<align>` + `<pointers>`):
    1. Open all matched conditional `ref` specifications first (before editing or proposing a final design).
    2. State the six fields below without preamble and wait for operator confirmation before executing.
  - **Approved-Step Exemption Boundary:** Treat a step as already defined ONLY when it is a trivial `Route 0` typo/lookup OR the next bounded step of a multi-step plan whose `Goal`, `Tasks -> Subtasks`, `Output`, and constraints were explicitly confirmed by the operator without subsequent scope drift (`EM-11`). Unconfirmed prior analysis or exploration never self-authorizes skipping `<align>` (`AD-18`).
  - **IF** the task is a delegation or a session handover → **THEN** `EM-09` (`§5.1`) governs the 4D contract; this adapter supplies `Goal` decomposition and `Redraft` alignment before work begins.

### 8.1 The Six-Field Task Contract (Unified with `EM-10`)

State all six before work starts. Each field prevents a distinct execution failure:

- **Goal**: Concrete desired outcome and hard constraints. For multi-step or multi-module work, decompose into nested **`Tasks -> Subtasks`** before listing edits. Prevents fragmented effort and dropped secondary constraints (`SpecBench`).
- **Input**: Flowing context that feeds execution — opened conditional `ref` specs, authoritative sources with priority rank, verified assumptions, and explicit exclusions (what to ignore). **Never copy-paste the user's raw prompt verbatim.** Prevents redundant noise and missing upstream constraints.
- **Process**: How facts are gathered and **verified** (the exact command or inspection per claim), matched execution adapters, and the **named reasoning framework** if used. Prevents guessing from memory and opaque reasoning.
- **Skills**: The tools or skills to invoke, or explicit `none`. Prevents silent adoption of unrequested workflows.
- **Output**: Target changes on disk and deliverables produced, nested **per subtask** when `Goal` spans multiple subtasks. Prevents status reports substituting for real changes.
- **Redraft**: Compact, explicitly disposable preview **by example** — user story, outline, `Given-When-Then` scenario, or sample diff — nested **per subtask** when multi-step and scaled by `EM-06a` (`L0–L3`). Prevents spending execution budget on the wrong mental model.

**Assumptions live inside whichever field depends on them**, never in a trailing footnote. A non-trivial specification claiming zero assumptions usually skipped reading its sources closely.

### 8.2 Scaled `Redraft` & Value Delivery (`EM-06a`)

Match `Redraft` depth to decision stakes and reversibility ([qa-decision-matrix.md](qa-decision-matrix.md) §2.3) so alignment stays high-signal without causing token bloat:

- **`L0` (Routine & Reversible Single Step):** Skip formal redrafting; execute directly (`Route 0`).
- **`L1` (Medium Scope):** One compact outline or brief user story showing section structure and intent per task.
- **`L2` (`Impact >= 80`):** One concrete worked example or `Given-When-Then` acceptance slice per subtask built from real repository data or artifacts.
- **`L3` (High-Risk / Irreversible / Cross-Feature):** Multiple scenarios or failure-edge walkthroughs per subtask with explicit fixture checks before execution begins.

A rejected redraft is the adapter succeeding cheaply before code or prose churn occurs.

### 8.3 Named Reasoning Framework Declaration Inside `Process`

When a task uses a logical or business reasoning framework, **`Process` names it explicitly** so the reader can inspect, challenge, or reproduce the method. *(Verified 2026-11-11 across `apex-meta/informatics/`, `AI-Snippets/`, and local QMD collections: no closed internal framework ranking study exists; use this practical taxonomy and never invent composite ranking scores per `WP-07`.)*

- **Root-Cause & Decomposition:** First Principles breakdown, 5-Whys causal chain.
- **Sequencing & Architecture:** Dependency / Critical Path ordering, Macro-Meso-Micro (`EM-10`).
- **Communication & Product Shaping:** SCQA / Minto BLUF (`WP-12`), User Story Mapping (`Goal -> Tasks -> Subtasks`).
- **Evaluation & Trade-Offs:** Q&A Decision Matrix (`EM-06`), 4-Phase Bake-Off (`EM-07`).
- **Adversarial Verification:** Premortem / Inversion (`FixedBench`-style negative check).

### 8.4 Relationship to Neighbouring Rules

- `<align>` + `<pointers>` in Layer 1 enforce cross-harness pre-action ref reads and 6-field alignment across Claude, Codex, and Gemini without relying on Claude-only hooks (`EM-13` detail lives here).
- `EM-09` §5.1 owns subagent/session handoffs and `EM-14` (`handover.md`) owns step close-out `Continuation` proposals referencing prior reasoning by `path#heading`; never duplicate schemas across adapters (`WP-23`).
- `EM-10` (`iterative-execution.md`) reuses this identical 6-field schema for Route 1 / Route 2 preflights.
- `EM-02` still governs: resolve immediately checkable questions with tools rather than specifying around them.

### 8.5 Task Specification Failure Modes & Not-To-Dos (`WP-25`)

- **Never copy-paste the user prompt into `Input`:** Extract flowing sources, `ref` specs, assumptions, and exclusions while expressing intent in `Goal`.
- **Never skip matched conditional `ref` reads before acting:** Two-phase alignment requires opening matched `ref` files prior to editing or proposing final architecture.
- **Never treat unconfirmed prior analysis as an "approved step":** Only explicit operator confirmation or trivial `Route 0` typos/lookups bypass `<align>`.
- **Never inflate low-risk tasks with `L3` ceremony:** Keep `Redraft` depth proportional to stakes via `EM-06a`.

- **EM-14 [P0 | I92/E95/R07] Major Step Close-Out & Continuation**:
  - **IF** completing a major step or multi-step phase → **THEN** execute all four close-out steps below before declaring completion or proposing follow-up work:
    1. **Verify:** Check every stated requirement and target gate directly against the modified artifacts (`<target>`, `AD-01`). If an operating artifact owns the change, verify that file itself reflects the update.
    2. **Scoped Stage, Commit & Push (`EM-12`):** When delivery includes repo persistence or sync, stage explicitly scoped paths (`git add -- <paths>`), commit, and push (`git pull --rebase` on non-fast-forward).
    3. **Update Owning & Working Files:** Mark completed tasks/decisions in the living working plan and canonical operating artifact so later steps or chats never repeat finished work (`FA-01`).
    4. **Propose Next 6-Field `Continuation`:** Draft the next step using the unified 6-field contract (`Goal` w/ `Tasks -> Subtasks`, flowing `Input`, `Process`, `Skills`, `Output`, `Redraft` per [task-specification.md](task-specification.md) §8.1), linking prior established reasoning by `path#heading` instead of restating solved analysis (`<context>`, `WP-23`).

### 5.4 Scoped Git Preflight Guard

- Never halt a step close-out on a blanket `git status --porcelain` check over unrelated dirty workspace files.
- Scope preflight status inspection to target deliverables and their direct dependencies (`git status --short -- <target_paths>`); preserve unrelated dirty files untouched (`EM-12`).

### 5.5 Handover & Close-Out Failure Modes & Not-To-Dos (`WP-25`)

- **Never write a handover to escape resolvable work (`EM-02`):** Invoke tools and answer checkable questions in the active turn.
- **Never rewrite already-settled prior reasoning inside a `Continuation`:** Reference the authoritative rationale via `path#heading` links.
- **Never mark a rule or design change Done inside quotes or handovers alone:** Update the owning canonical operating file first (`FA-01`).
- **Never abort a scoped push or close-out over unrelated dirty workspace files:** Check only target paths and keep adjacent work untouched.

## Procedure

1. **Load routing context.** Read the operator task, prompt packet, flow packet, expected output type, workflow context, AI surface inventory, quota map, model usage summary, and usage delta when available; mark missing inputs without blocking unless routing cannot be estimated.

2. **Classify task value.** Assign routing mode, cost class, risk level, evidence need, ambiguity, and high_end_reasoning_score using the task impact and downstream consequences.

3. **Select surface.** Choose the best stable surface class and fallback surface for the task, using quality and risk first for planned flow sessions and leverage-weighted cost efficiency for supplemental or batch work.

4. **Plan usage.** Create a planned usage budget that states expected scarcity pressure, whether scarce or high-end modes are justified, and what usage fields must be captured later.

5. **Create recommendation.** Produce a routing recommendation packet containing routing_decision, planned_usage_budget, usage_tracking_tags, quota_rationale, fallback_rule, and operator_review_flags.

6. **Resolve conflicts.** If operator preference, workflow fit, prompt quality, and cost disagree, apply the authority order operator decision, workflow fit, prompt quality, then routing cost; surface unresolved conflicts as an operator tradeoff card.

7. **Validate boundaries.** Confirm that the recommendation does not execute prompts, create project plans, create calendar events, define workflow/process taxonomies, or finalize volatile provider/model/pricing claims.

8. **Prepare feedback hook.** State how FlowRecap or later usage logs should report actual usage_delta so future routing recommendations can compare planned use with actual use.

## Failure Modes

```yaml
failure_modes:
  missing_AI_surface_inventory:
    trigger: "No AI_surface_inventory is supplied or the inventory lacks usable surface classes."
    correction: "Use provider_unspecified with stable abstract surface classes and mark validation_status as low_confidence_auto_generated."

  missing_quota_map:
    trigger: "No monthly_quota_map or model_usage_summary is supplied for a quota-sensitive decision."
    correction: "Create a conservative planned_usage_budget and add operator_review_flags for missing quota context."

  volatile_provider_claim_requested:
    trigger: "The task requires current pricing, exact model rankings, product limits, or availability."
    correction: "Do not claim the value; require current verification or mark the claim as unknown."

  cost_overrides_quality:
    trigger: "The route selects a cheaper surface even though impact, risk, evidence need, or ambiguity justify stronger reasoning."
    correction: "Re-rank the route using the planned_flow_session priority order and explain the tradeoff."

  prompt_execution_requested:
    trigger: "The operator asks this skill to run the prompt rather than route it."
    correction: "Return the routing recommendation only and state that prompt execution is out of scope."

  workflow_conflict_detected:
    trigger: "The selected route conflicts with workflow stage, process stage, or expected output type."
    correction: "Defer to workflow-process-design validation and mark operator_review_recommended."

  operator_choice_conflict:
    trigger: "The operator explicitly chooses a provider or surface that conflicts with routing recommendations."
    correction: "Preserve operator choice, show the risk/cost/quality tradeoff, and flag the conflict."

  final_model_map_drift:
    trigger: "The output tries to finalize OpenRouter or exact model mapping."
    correction: "Replace exact mapping with TODO placeholder classes and keep API use supplemental by default."
```

## Procedure

1. **Load planning context.** Read the operator request, supplied notes, project goal, prior planning context, and any existing task records; if no usable project context exists, apply the `no_project_context` failure mode.

2. **Capture the project.** Convert source material into a project capture record with goal, scope, constraints, source, and review flags, without creating or mutating durable files.

3. **Define the epic container.** Draft an epic record for `apex-meta/epics/<slug>/` when the request introduces a new project-level work container, and mark unresolved scope decisions for operator review.

4. **Decompose work.** Produce proposed task records using the canonical task fields from `references/task-record-contract.md`, preserving the status enum, priority policy, due_date field, depends_on field, blocked_by field, acceptance criteria, definition of done, notes, and source.

5. **Propose dependencies.** Assign only dependency proposals in `depends_on`, flag obvious circular dependency risk, and mark uncertain or incomplete dependency evidence for apex-sync validation.

6. **Explain priority, urgency, and focus.** Assign high, medium, or low priority with rationale, record due_date when known, explain urgency qualitatively, and draft only a provisional focus recommendation.

7. **Gate and hand off.** Present the planning packet, review flags, and handoff requests to the operator; do not mutate state, and route exact ranking or validation to apex-sync and any confirmed write or status mutation to apex-session.

## Procedure

1. **Classify the request.** Decide whether the operator is asking for session update, handoff creation, state delta extraction, entity update records, status mutation validation, or next-session context. If the request asks for new decomposition, route to `apex-plan`. If it asks for ranking, blocker scan, registry rebuild, drift detection, stale detection, or score computation, route to `apex-sync`.

2. **Read before deciding.** Inspect the provided task/session evidence, prior H6 files, raw source references, handoff notes, and operator instructions before drafting any final artifact. Preserve missing or unresolved context as explicit review flags instead of filling gaps from memory.

3. **Preserve source basis.** Carry every available `raw_source_ref` and `raw_source_path` into the relevant state delta, entity update, findings, or progress entry. If raw source evidence is expected but absent, set `review_flags` to include `raw_source_missing`.

4. **Validate status values.** For every requested status change, check `status_before` and `status_after` against the exact H1 enum: `open`, `in-progress`, `blocked`, `done`, `deferred`. Reject any other task status value with `review_flags: [invalid_status]`.

5. **Create mutation records.** For each valid status change, create a `status_mutation_record` and a `before_after_preview` using the schemas in `references/mutation-gate-rules.md`. Include `status_change_reason`, `operator_validation`, `validation_status`, and `validation_timestamp`.

6. **Apply the operator validation gate.** Consequential mutations must have `operator_validation: confirmed` before they are treated as confirmed records. If validation is missing, rejected, or needs revision, keep the record visible but not confirmed and add the appropriate review flag.

7. **Extract state deltas.** Convert session evidence into `state_delta_summary` records. Capture what changed, what remained unresolved, which raw sources support the change, and whether any `source_conflict` exists.

8. **Maintain entity update records.** Create `entity_update_record` entries when the session reveals durable changes to projects, tasks, artifacts, concepts, people, tools, or source references. Flag `duplicate_entity_risk` or `source_conflict` instead of silently merging uncertain entities.

9. **Produce H6 handoff artifacts.** Generate or refresh the final artifact set: `task_plan.md`, `findings.md`, `progress.md`, and `next-session.md`. Ensure `next-session.md` contains exactly these sections: Current Step, Open Items, Risks, Decisions Made, Next Actions.

10. **Create planning feed.** Produce `planning_feed` as clean input for the planning layer. Include next-session context, durable findings, open items, risks, decisions made, raw source references, and review flags. Do not compute final rank or exact focus candidate.

11. **Validate completion.** Check the final outputs against the validation rules below and the package manifest. If any gate fails, revise the affected file content before returning the result.

## APEX OS Backbone Role

`apex-sync` is the deterministic-computation capability in the shared Plan-Sync-Session Backbone. Multi-Agent Orchestration may invoke it through Meta Ops; Weekly Orchestrator may read relevant confirmed reports by reference. Running or reading a Sync report does not activate either orchestration system.

## Objective

`apex-sync` computes deterministic read-side synchronization reports over Apex
task files. It reads task frontmatter and Markdown body content under
`apex-meta/epics/`, validates dependency and status consistency, and delegates
all exact computation to the canonical Python command at `scripts/apex_sync.py`.
It may write only `apex-meta/registry/index.md`, only through the `registry`
subcommand, and only when the operator explicitly uses `--dry-run false`.
It does not capture new projects, decompose work, mutate task status, author
handoff files, validate operator decisions, or create session narrative.

## Global boundaries

- Never auto-trigger a skill or orchestration system without operator intent.
- Never infer, default, or fabricate operator confirmation.
- An explicitly requested autonomous run may batch interaction, but it never fabricates confirmation or performs confirmed mutation outside the selected entrypoint's gate contract.

- Load `.repair-backups/`, recovery, staging, verification, report, and validation-report directories only when the operator explicitly requests the relevant recovery or audit task.
- Never create cron jobs, schedulers, Kanban tasks, or calendar events automatically.
- On missing or unsafe input, follow the selected entrypoint's failure contract and report the unresolved condition.

## 4. Review model (Q8 + research P2)

Two blind parallel lenses (validity, strategic alignment) as fresh `meta-detective` invocations; criterion-level falsification mandatory; deterministic aggregation (`escalate > needs_input > hold > revise > pass`, single critical non-pass blocks, no majority vote, no LLM aggregator); reviewer never fixes; correction = new immutable version = re-review. ## 1. Topology (Q1, Q2)

File-backed workflow + tool-scoped subagents. Four durable **accountabilities** — Alfred (operator interface), Meta Strategy (macro direction), Meta Ops (meso workflow + shared-backbone integration), Meta Detective (independent review) — plus three **specialist lanes** (Knowledge Bank, Informatics Design, Prompts & Workflows) and unbounded one-off **domain workers**. The definitions are durable; role adoption and spawned workers are run-scoped. None holds authoritative state between runs — state is in files.

The Plan-Sync-Session Backbone is shared APEX OS infrastructure, not a third orchestration system and not owned by Multi-Agent Orchestration. Inside an active run, Meta Ops uses it as follows: `apex-plan` proposes and decomposes, `apex-sync` computes deterministically, and `apex-session` applies confirmed mutation and closure. The old Apex v2 swarm is translated (its invariants survive as fields, workflows, and law), not revived (no 9 always-on agents, no BUILD/VERIFY/LOCK engine).

```
OPERATOR ⇄ Alfred
             │
  Meta Strategy (options; operator selects)
             │
  Meta Ops ──── apex-plan → apex-sync → [lanes/workers] → integrate
     │                                                        │
     ├────────── detective-review (validity ∥ alignment) ◄────┘
     │                    │ verdicts → named owners
     └── operator gate → apex-session (confirmed mutation) → state delta / next session
```

## 2. Runtime mapping (mechanism ladder — smallest sufficient rung)

**Invocation modes (load-bearing):** **Alfred and Meta Ops are main-conversation contracts** adopted only inside an explicitly started Multi-Agent Orchestration run. Alfred remains in the main conversation for live operator dialogue and exact decision capture. Meta Ops remains there to hold the complete run sequence, gate records, integration state, and closure across phases. **Meta Strategy, Meta Detective, the three lanes, and domain workers are spawned only when the active workflow routes a bounded packet to them.** Custom subagent skills and delegation capabilities are explicit runtime configuration, not an activation signal; the presence of a file under `.claude/agents/` never makes a role global or always active.

## 3. Permission model (Q6, Q7, Q8 + research P1)

Role names grant nothing. Permission derives from state, on three axes:

1. **`lifecycle_stage`** (packet): `proposal` → `computed` → `confirmed`. Only apex-session writes `confirmed`.

## 2. Canonical Operational Decisions (The Decision Register)

| Decision ID | Operational Domain | Formal Decision | Empirical Grounding & Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **DEC-QMD-01** | **Search Speed Policy** | **Two-Tier Escalation:** Agents MUST run `qmd search` (FTS5 BM25) first. Escalation to `qmd query` (hybrid AI reranking) is authorized ONLY when keyword search yields zero results. | Measured latency: `qmd search` executes in **0.32 seconds**; `qmd query` takes **19 to 44 seconds** (130x latency differential). `RESULTS-09`. |
| **DEC-QMD-02** | **Windows Daemon Policy** | **Direct CLI Execution Only:** On Windows, all agents MUST invoke `qmd` via direct terminal commands. Running `qmd mcp --daemon` or `--http --daemon` is banned. | Audit of `@tobilu/qmd/dist/cli/mcp-pid.js`: relies on Unix process inspection, causing orphaned zombie processes on Windows. |
| **DEC-QMD-03** | **Index Scope Bounding** | **Final-Only Workstation Bounding:** The local QMD collection (`apex-informatics-final`) indexes only `apex-meta/informatics/final/**.md`. | `FA-03` [Five-Plane Separation], `AD-04` [Context Hygiene]. Keeps the index tightly focused on active specs and research. |
| **DEC-QMD-04** | **Surgical Slicing Discipline** | **Mandatory Slice Fetching:** Agents MUST use `qmd get "#docid:from:count"` or `qmd get path:line:count` to pull 20–40 line windows. Bulk whole-file reads are forbidden. | `AD-04`, `AD-19`. Consumes <10% of full-file token budgets; prevents LLM cognitive overload and attention drift. |
| **DEC-QMD-05** | **Structured Query Document Authoring** | **Negative Space Intent Formulation:** When `qmd query` is required, agents MUST supply typed query documents (`intent:` + `lex:` + `vec:`) to bypass the 11.8s expansion phase. | Prevents Tobias Lütke 1.7B expansion model from drifting on specialized research terms. Cuts query latency by 57%. |
| **DEC-QMD-06** | **Index Refresh Cadence** | **On-Demand & Git Hook Sync:** Re-indexing is triggered on-demand via `qmd update` when documentation changes. Unchanged files are skipped via SHA-256 content hashing. | Incremental hashing takes <2 seconds when no files have changed. |

1. **Locate the loop.** Read the latest confirmed Session planning feed and relevant Sync reports, then list the newest files in `artifacts/weekly-plans/`, `artifacts/next-day-plans/`, `artifacts/flow-packets/`, and `artifacts/flow-recap-packets/`. The newest confirmed packet determines the current stage; report loop position in ≤5 lines before dispatching anything.
2. **Dispatch a stage.** Invoke the stage's owning Skill directly in its own isolated fork (`execution: context: fork` declared on the Skill itself — no wrapper agent in between) with a dispatch prompt containing exactly: the input packet paths, the operator's stage-specific intent, any confirmed constraints, and always `run_date` (YYYYMMDD) plus, for planning stages, `week_id` — a forked Skill assumes no parent-context knowledge (`parent_context_assumed: false`) and cannot determine dates itself. Do not paste packet contents — paths only (refs not copies). The two review stages (`apex-review-validity`, `apex-review-alignment`) remain independent Subagents dispatched via the Agent mechanism, not Skill forks — see step 4.
   - Parallel dispatch: evidence_normalize and flow_recap invocations for different flows of the same day are independent — dispatch them concurrently (one forked Skill worker per flow). Review lens pairs always run in parallel. Planning stages and status_merge never run concurrently with each other.
3. **Receive the return.** A stage return is the handoff envelope + short summary. Validate the envelope against `references/handoff-schema.md` (all required fields present, `expected_action` and `stop_condition` non-empty, `target_surface` correct per field_rules). An invalid envelope goes back to the same stage worker (Skill fork, or reviewer agent) once with the named gaps; a second failure halts the stage and reports.
4. **Trigger review when consequential.** Apply the trigger test in `references/review-wiring.md`. If triggered: freeze digest, dispatch both reviewers in parallel with blind packets, aggregate deterministically, update `authority.state` accordingly. 5. **Hold the gate.** Present the stage summary and the exact gate question to the operator; record the answer by updating the packet's `operator_validation` field and gate date. Gate passage lives in the packet file, never only in chat.
6. **Route confirmed changes.** After G5 confirmation, hand the approved status_merge_packet and its evidence references to `apex-session`. Session alone validates and applies the project/task mutation, produces the mutation receipt, and refreshes the planning feed. Do not write `state/` files or project-task records from this skill.
7. **Advance.** Report the next stage and its trigger in one line. Never auto-trigger the next planning stage — the loop advances on operator trigger (or within an explicitly requested autonomous run).

## Failure behavior

failure_modes:
  stage_worker_returns_blocked: report the named missing inputs, offer the skill's degraded mode if it has one, continue with the next independent stage if any.
  project_engine_context_missing: continue in degraded mode at low confidence; flag missing Session or Sync context to the operator; never reconstruct accepted truth from candidates.
  envelope_invalid_twice: halt that stage, keep its output as `invalidated`, report.
  operator_absent_in_autonomous_run: produce all packets with `operator_validation: not_requested`, batch-present gates at run end; never fabricate confirmation; never apply canon writes.
  unsafe_write_condition: halt and report — this overrides any autonomous-run instruction.
